clue.text: Letters from abroad and when they might arrive?

blocks.note: first meaning: characters of the Greek alphabet, foreign letters
second meaning: estimated times of arrival, abbreviated in the plural

explanation.surface: Someone abroad is wondering when their letters home will reach the recipients.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests overseas post; one meaning is Greek letters, the other the travel abbreviation ETA, estimated time of arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is a Greek character, and an ETA is the predicted moment a traveller or delivery turns up.

clue.text: Uplifting place hosting jazz quartets

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something up means reading it from the bottom upwards
a host has guests inside, so this word holds the next piece within it

blocks.note: to place something is to set it down
trad is traditional jazz

explanation.surface: An inspiring venue puts on jazz quartets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' reads as praise for the venue, but in a down clue it turns the word for place upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrad is a group or set of four, so tetrads are quartets in the general numerical sense.

clue.text: It may be wound and fastened at the front

definitions.text: It may be wound and fastened at the front

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a scar is the mark a wound leaves, standing for the wound itself
the opening letter of fastened

explanation.surface: Something is wrapped round and secured at the front, like a winter accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the answer; 'wound' also works as the past tense of wind, the way this garment is put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarf is wrapped round the neck several times and often knotted or pinned at the front.

clue.text: A line taken by a green conservation group concerning food

indicators.note: what is taken by someone goes along after them, so the first phrase comes after the second

blocks.note: taken as written
lime is a shade of green
the National Trust, which conserves historic British buildings and land
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: An environmental pressure group adopts an official policy on food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken by' means the phrase 'A line' goes after the group, not inside it. The National Trust is a British heritage and countryside charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Alimentary means relating to nourishment or digestion, as in the alimentary canal.

clue.text: PM of old drafted in following refusal from Brussels

indicators.note: something drafted in is brought inside to join a group, so it sits within another piece

blocks.note: following means coming after
the French word for no, as spoken in Brussels
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister is brought in after a rejection from the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like a Prime Minister, and Brussels like the EU; PM is really post meridiem, and Brussels just supplies the French no.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, from Latin post meridiem, marks the hours after midday, which is the afternoon.

clue.text: It’s at the crease their bats get left

indicators.note: bats as an adjective means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: in cricket a batsman at the crease is in
the letters of their, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: at the crease, the players' bats get left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture makes 'bats' a noun; it is the adjective meaning mad. The crease is where a batter stands in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To inherit is to receive money or property bequeathed in a will, that is, to be left it.

clue.text: Dye one used in one’s pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so these letters are in a poor, jumbled state
something used in a mixture is put inside it

blocks.note: the letters of the word, ignoring the apostrophe
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone has dyed their own underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as underwear but is British slang for rubbish, a scramble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eosin is a red fluorescent dye used to stain tissue samples in microscopy.

clue.text: At Tosca, playing in Lyon, he wears formal garments

indicators.note: playing about with something means moving it around, so these letters are rearranged
whoever wears a garment is inside it, so this piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the letters of the two words
il is French for he, as in the French city of Lyon

explanation.surface: A man in Lyon dresses formally when Tosca is being performed at the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosca is Puccini's opera, which suits 'playing', but here it is only letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailcoats are men's formal evening jackets, cut short at the front with long tails behind.

clue.text: Ruling expecting a child to doff its cap

indicators.note: doffing a cap takes off what is on top, so the opening letter goes

blocks.note: an expectant mother is with child

explanation.surface: A ruling about a pregnant woman removing her hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnant describes a monarch actually reigning, as in queen regnant, so it means ruling.

clue.text: Sound not diluted by speakers

indicators.note: what speakers say is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its pronunciation

blocks.note: a drink taken undiluted is taken straight

explanation.surface: Speakers deliver a sound that has not been watered down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' suggests noise next to 'speakers'; it is a channel of sea, as in Puget Sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound and a strait are both narrow stretches of sea between two land masses.

clue.text: Things not right about American election events

indicators.note: something not right is wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged
about means around, so these letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Something has gone wrong at American election events.
explanation.definitionFit: Hustings are meetings where candidates address voters during a campaign, a British term for campaign events.

clue.text: Traveller that’s much less biased we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the phrase is taken by its pronunciation

blocks.note: way means much, and fairer means less biased

explanation.surface: A tourist is said to be far more impartial than others.
explanation.definitionFit: A wayfarer is someone journeying on foot, an old word for a person on the road.

clue.text: Drink mostly tea or periodically something sweeter

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is lost
periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: to neck a drink is to swallow it quickly
the first, third and fifth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone drinks tea most of the time, or now and then a sweeter alternative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' looks like the definition, but it is the verb neck; the definition is the sweet thing at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the sugary liquid in flowers that bees collect, a byword for something deliciously sweet.

clue.text: Finest people categorised as AB, not out of this world

blocks.note: an AB, able seaman, is a sailor, and an old salt is a sailor
what is not out of this world belongs to it

explanation.surface: The best people are classed as blood group AB, perfectly ordinary and down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: AB looks like a blood group or grade; it is able seaman, a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from the Sermon on the Mount, describes good, honest, decent folk of great worth.

clue.text: Pine variety spanning great distances

blocks.note: to pine for something is to long for it
a range is a variety or assortment

explanation.surface: A kind of pine tree whose branches reach a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' and 'variety' suggest a type of tree; pine is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-range describes missiles, forecasts or flights that cover a great distance.

clue.text: Remove a goddess after her first heartless command

indicators.note: taking only what comes after her opening letter means that letter is dropped
without a heart means the central letter is taken out

blocks.note: Hera is the queen of the Greek gods
a dictate is an order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get rid of a goddess following her initial cruel order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' suggests a cruel order; it removes the middle T of the seven-letter command.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out or get rid of something completely, like removing it at the root.

clue.text: Chances to learn about girls after getting flat

indicators.note: one thing after another means it follows on, so the earlier words come later

blocks.note: evening a surface is making it flat
C stands for circa, about
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Girls seeking chances to learn once they've moved into their own flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment, but here it is the adjective, as in making a surface level.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening classes are adult education courses held at night, giving grown-ups opportunities for study.

clue.text: He managed to score every season

definitions.text: He managed to score every season

blocks.clueFragment: He managed to score every season
blocks.note: surface reading: a football or cricket manager whose team found the net in every campaign
setter's reading: a composer who wrote music for spring, summer, autumn and winter, The Four Seasons

explanation.walkthrough: Score means compose music for, and the seasons are the four violin concertos of the famous Baroque work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian Baroque composer wrote The Four Seasons, a set of concertos depicting each time of year.

clue.text: Old instrument: it keeps time in a research facility

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the next piece goes inside
in places the preceding group inside the following one

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
CERN is the European particle physics laboratory near Geneva

explanation.surface: An antique instrument keeps the beat in a scientific laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: IT holds T at its end, and that block sits inside the laboratory's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The cittern is a wire-strung Renaissance instrument of the guitar family, now largely obsolete.

clue.text: Underwear being worn prolongs a visit

blocks.note: stays are an old word for a corset
clothes being worn are on

explanation.surface: A guest keeps their underwear on and lingers longer than planned.
explanation.walkthrough: Stays are a stiffened corset, an old-fashioned undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays on remains somewhere beyond the expected time, extending their visit.

clue.text: Notice daughter’s left before son heads off

indicators.note: the daughter has gone, so her abbreviation is removed from the word
coming before means the first piece is placed ahead of the next

blocks.note: an advert is a public notice
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent notices the daughter has gone out before the son sets off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads off' looks like the son leaving; it is the definition, meaning prevents.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a danger is to prevent it or turn it aside, just as heading it off does.

clue.text: Hurt as vehicles overturned

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, so in a down clue the word reads from the bottom

blocks.note: trams are vehicles on rails

explanation.surface: People were injured when vehicles turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to sting or feel sharp pain, the verb sense of being hurt.

clue.text: Court case features turning point

indicators.note: something that features a thing includes it, so the next piece goes inside
turning round means the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a court case is a trial
the nub is the central point of a matter

explanation.surface: A legal case hinges on a turning point.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a judicial body or court set up to settle particular disputes.

clue.text: Speak about territorial displays

indicators.note: the neighbouring words put the letters on show inside themselves

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone talks about animals' territorial displays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a reversal or container signal; it simply contributes its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say something aloud or voice it, so it means speak.

clue.text: Stretch one leg out introducing a tango

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so these letters are rearranged
introducing something brings it in, so the next piece goes inside

blocks.note: the letters of the two words
taken as written
tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dancer extends one leg as the tango begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to make longer by pulling or extending, the same as lengthening.

clue.text: Witness attending trial

blocks.note: to be at an event is to attend it
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A witness is present at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The courtroom picture makes 'trial' a legal hearing; here it is a test.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness formally, declaring that something is true or genuine.

clue.text: Amateur puzzling title held by a poet

indicators.note: something puzzling is confused, so these letters are mixed up
what is held by something sits inside its grasp

blocks.note: taken as written
Dante Alighieri, the medieval Italian poet

explanation.surface: A poet has been given a baffling title.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in an art or subject without serious commitment, a mere dabbler rather than professional.

clue.text: Sheer class

blocks.note: first meaning: utter, downright
second meaning: a level or grade in a hierarchy

explanation.walkthrough: Sheer class sounds like a compliment; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means complete or unmitigated; as a noun it means a position or grade in society or the army.
